MTX_WEEKLY.title: Low-dose methotrexate dosing for inflammatory disease
MTX_WEEKLY.summary: UpToDate clinical drug information describes low-dose methotrexate regimens for inflammatory disorders using a weekly administration schedule. This prototype uses the weekly-vs-daily distinction to detect a potential frequency/order-entry error.
MTX_WEEKLY.verification: Verify the patient's indication, formulation, intended weekly dose, and current authorized reference before acting.

MTX_DOSE_ANOMALY.title: Methotrexate — patient-specific dosing and monitoring
MTX_DOSE_ANOMALY.summary: Methotrexate dosing depends on indication, formulation, response, toxicity, and patient factors. The prototype intentionally flags an unusual dose for verification rather than declaring a universal maximum or automatically selecting a replacement dose.
MTX_DOSE_ANOMALY.verification: Check the current licensed reference for the exact indication and formulation.

GLARGINE_FREQUENCY.title: Insulin glargine — basal insulin administration
GLARGINE_FREQUENCY.summary: UpToDate describes insulin glargine as a basal insulin generally administered once daily in standard regimens. A TID entry can therefore represent a potential frequency/order-entry anomaly requiring verification.
GLARGINE_FREQUENCY.verification: Confirm the insulin product, concentration, regimen, and clinical context.

HEPARIN_NUMERIC_ANOMALY.title: Context-dependent anticoagulant order verification
HEPARIN_NUMERIC_ANOMALY.summary: Unfractionated heparin doses vary by indication, route, protocol, and patient-specific factors. A large number alone should not be treated as proof of error; the safe prototype behavior is contextual verification.
HEPARIN_NUMERIC_ANOMALY.verification: Use the current authorized anticoagulation protocol/reference for the exact indication.

ISMP_LEADING_ZERO.title: ISMP List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024)
ISMP_LEADING_ZERO.summary: ISMP recommends a leading zero before a decimal point for doses less than one unit because a naked decimal can be missed.
ISMP_LEADING_ZERO.verification: Apply the current organizational medication-writing standard where applicable.

ISMP_TRAILING_ZERO.title: ISMP List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024)
ISMP_TRAILING_ZERO.summary: ISMP recommends avoiding trailing zeros for whole-number doses because a decimal point can be missed and create a tenfold error.
ISMP_TRAILING_ZERO.verification: Apply the current organizational medication-writing standard where applicable.

INSULIN_UNIT.title: Insulin dose-unit plausibility
INSULIN_UNIT.summary: The prototype checks for a unit mismatch such as insulin entered in mg rather than units. This is an order-entry plausibility check, not a dosing recommendation.
INSULIN_UNIT.verification: Verify product, concentration, dose unit, and intended number of units.

ROUTE_MISMATCH.title: Route/formulation plausibility
ROUTE_MISMATCH.summary: The prototype compares selected route with a small set of standard route expectations and flags potential mismatches for verification.
ROUTE_MISMATCH.verification: Confirm the actual formulation and intended route in an authorized reference.

RENAL_REVIEW.title: Renal function and medication assessment
RENAL_REVIEW.summary: Renal function can materially affect the safety or dosing of several medications. The prototype flags the need for patient-specific review rather than generating an automatic dose.
RENAL_REVIEW.verification: Check the current patient-specific renal dosing recommendation in an authorized reference.

HEPATIC_REVIEW.title: Hepatic function and medication assessment
HEPATIC_REVIEW.summary: Abnormal liver tests can be clinically relevant to medication selection, safety, or monitoring for some drugs. The prototype uses them as a verification trigger rather than an automatic dose adjustment.
HEPATIC_REVIEW.verification: Review the current drug-specific hepatic safety and monitoring information.

MTX_TMP_SMX.source: UpToDate Drug Interaction / licensed drug-reference workflow
MTX_TMP_SMX.title: Methotrexate and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole interaction
MTX_TMP_SMX.summary: This combination can create clinically important toxicity concerns and should trigger deliberate interaction review and verification.
MTX_TMP_SMX.verification: Check the current interaction monograph and patient-specific factors.

ALLERGY_MATCH.title: Allergy-to-order cross-check
ALLERGY_MATCH.summary: The prototype checks whether the entered allergy text appears to match the selected drug and flags a potential safety issue for verification.
ALLERGY_MATCH.verification: Confirm the allergy history, reaction, severity, and intended medication.

MISSING_WEIGHT.title: Missing patient weight
MISSING_WEIGHT.summary: Some medications require weight-based assessment. The prototype flags missing weight instead of guessing it.
MISSING_WEIGHT.verification: Obtain a current weight when required for the medication-specific assessment.

PEDIATRIC_CONTEXT.title: Pediatric medication dosing requires age- and weight-specific assessment
PEDIATRIC_CONTEXT.summary: Pediatric dosing can depend on age, weight, indication, formulation, and medication-specific maximum doses. The prototype uses this as a verification prompt rather than generating an automatic pediatric dose.
PEDIATRIC_CONTEXT.verification: Verify current age/weight-based dosing and maximum dose in the authorized pediatric reference.

PEDIATRIC_REVIEW.title: Pediatric dosing context
PEDIATRIC_REVIEW.summary: The prototype flags pediatric orders for age- and weight-specific verification and does not assume adult dosing applies.
PEDIATRIC_REVIEW.verification: Confirm the medication-specific pediatric regimen using an authorized reference.

GERIATRIC_REVIEW.title: Geriatric medication review
GERIATRIC_REVIEW.summary: Older adults may require medication-specific review of renal function, pharmacokinetics, polypharmacy, and precautions. The prototype flags this for verification rather than automatically changing the order.
GERIATRIC_REVIEW.verification: Review the medication in the context of age, renal function, indication, and concomitant medications.

POTASSIUM_REVIEW.source: Hospital-approved electrolyte protocol / authorized drug reference
POTASSIUM_REVIEW.title: Potassium-related medication order verification
POTASSIUM_REVIEW.summary: An abnormal potassium value can materially affect the safety of electrolyte replacement and other medication orders. The prototype uses a screening trigger and does not calculate a replacement dose.
POTASSIUM_REVIEW.verification: Verify the latest potassium result, indication, ordered dose/concentration, route, and administration parameters against the current protocol.

MAGNESIUM_REVIEW.source: Hospital-approved electrolyte protocol / authorized drug reference
MAGNESIUM_REVIEW.title: Magnesium-related medication order verification
MAGNESIUM_REVIEW.summary: An abnormal magnesium value may affect the safety and urgency of electrolyte replacement. The prototype flags the order for contextual verification.
MAGNESIUM_REVIEW.verification: Verify the latest magnesium result and the ordered product, dose, concentration, route, and administration parameters.

CALCIUM_REVIEW.source: Hospital-approved electrolyte protocol / authorized drug reference
CALCIUM_REVIEW.title: Calcium-related medication order verification
CALCIUM_REVIEW.summary: Abnormal calcium values can require medication-specific contextual assessment. The prototype does not automatically recommend a replacement dose.
CALCIUM_REVIEW.verification: Verify laboratory value, clinical indication, formulation, dose, route, and administration parameters.

SODIUM_REVIEW.source: Hospital-approved electrolyte protocol / authorized clinical reference
SODIUM_REVIEW.title: Sodium-related medication order verification
SODIUM_REVIEW.summary: Abnormal sodium values can materially affect medication and fluid-management decisions. The prototype flags the context for clinical verification.
SODIUM_REVIEW.verification: Verify the latest sodium result and the indication, product, dose, route, and administration plan.

PHOSPHATE_REVIEW.source: Hospital-approved electrolyte protocol / authorized clinical reference
PHOSPHATE_REVIEW.title: Phosphate-related medication order verification
PHOSPHATE_REVIEW.summary: Abnormal phosphate values may require medication-specific assessment. The prototype uses a screening flag rather than an automatic replacement recommendation.
PHOSPHATE_REVIEW.verification: Verify laboratory value, indication, formulation, dose, route, and administration parameters.
